FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A22
Aggressive driving intentionally uses a driving action or traffic violation to endanger people or property. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A22
Speeding, tailgating and unsafe lane changes are examples associated with aggressive driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A22
Ignoring traffic controls or signaling improperly can be part of aggressive driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A22
Threats, hostile gestures and chasing another vehicle to cause harm are aggressive behaviors. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A22
To avoid aggressive driving, relax and concentrate on the driving task. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A22
Use the posted speed limit and plan a realistic travel time to reduce aggressive driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A22
Courteous and forgiving behavior helps prevent aggressive driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A22
Leave the area if possible and report serious aggressive behavior. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A22
Alcohol or other impairing drugs increase collision risk even in small amounts. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A22
People younger than 21 may not purchase, possess or drink alcoholic beverages. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A22
Alcohol and impairing drugs reduce perception, emergency response and vehicle-control ability. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A23
New drivers learning complex skills are especially affected by alcohol and impairing drugs. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A23
Alcohol and impairing drugs interfere with the brain functions used for judgment. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A23
Alcohol and some drugs can blur sight, delay focusing or cause double vision. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A23
Alcohol and impairing drugs reduce the ability to judge distance, speed and other vehicles' motion. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A23
Increasing impairment can lead to lane wandering, crossing the center line or leaving the road. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A23
The handbook states that vision is affected at a BAC of .02. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A23
Alcohol and impairing drugs can reduce the ability to tell road-sign and signal colors apart. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A23
Alcohol and impairing drugs slow information processing and responses to driving tasks. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A23
Alcohol and impairing drugs can cause drowsiness and reduce awareness of surroundings. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A23
Do not let a friend or relative drive after drinking. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A23
Taking a drinking person's keys is one way the handbook suggests preventing an impaired trip. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R23 | anchor: A23
Arrange a driver who has not been drinking for someone who consumed alcohol. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R24 | anchor: A23
A taxi is an alternative to letting a drinking person drive. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R25 | anchor: A23
An overnight stay is an alternative to driving after drinking. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R26 | anchor: A23
Coffee does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R27 | anchor: A23
Fresh air does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R28 | anchor: A23
A cold shower does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R29 | anchor: A23
Eating does not remove alcohol or other drugs from circulation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R30 | anchor: A23
The handbook identifies time as the medically established way for alcohol or drug combinations to leave circulation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R31 | anchor: A23
Even a first alcoholic drink can impair the ability to drive. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R32 | anchor: A23
The safest advice in the handbook is to avoid driving after consuming alcohol or impairing drugs. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R33 | anchor: A23
A BAC of .08 or greater violates the alcohol-driving law described in the handbook. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R34 | anchor: A23
For a BAC of .08 or higher, the handbook describes a possible 30-day suspension and criminal penalties. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R35 | anchor: A23
Kansas drivers below 21 can be arrested for alcohol impairment at a BAC of .02 percent. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R36 | anchor: A23
BAC expresses the proportion of alcohol relative to the amount of blood in the body. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R37 | anchor: A23
A driver can still be impaired and convicted of impaired driving below a BAC of .08. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec03-R38 | anchor: A24
An alcohol-concentration test usually uses breath, blood or urine to measure alcohol in the body. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R39 | anchor: A24
Kansas implied consent treats obtaining a license as agreement to a lawfully requested alcohol test when impaired driving is suspected. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R40 | anchor: A24
The handbook states that refusing an alcohol test can result in losing a license for one year. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R41 | anchor: A24
For a first alcohol conviction, the handbook lists a fine from 750 to 1000 dollars plus court costs. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R42 | anchor: A24
For a first alcohol conviction, the handbook lists at least 48 jail hours or 100 community-service hours. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R43 | anchor: A24
A first alcohol conviction carries license suspension under the handbook's description. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R44 | anchor: A24
The handbook requires an ignition-interlock device after a first alcohol conviction. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R45 | anchor: A24
Second and later alcohol convictions carry more severe penalties. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R46 | anchor: A24
Prescription and nonprescription drugs can impair driving as much as or more than alcohol. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R47 | anchor: A24
Some headache, cold, allergy and calming medicines cause drowsiness that affects driving. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R48 | anchor: A24
Stimulant and diet pills may cause dizziness, nervousness, concentration trouble or vision problems. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

Misconceptions: Coffee or a cold shower does not remove alcohol from the bloodstream; feeling more alert must not be treated as sober driving ability.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: sight, sleep, attention, substances, health and emotion; these words retrieve the cited fitness checks.
Glossary: Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness; distraction takes attention from driving; the BAC definition appears in a fact block.
Dynamic facts: Legal sanctions and test-refusal rules are revision-bound and require issuer refresh; undated crash statistics and fixed sober-up calculations are isolated as debt.

FACT_ID: sec03-R49 | anchor: A24
Read nonprescription drug warnings before taking the product. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R50 | anchor: A24
Ask a doctor or pharmacist about driving effects when a drug's safety is unclear. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R51 | anchor: A24
Prescription drugs may impair reflexes, judgment, sight and alertness. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R52 | anchor: A24
Antidepressants, pain medicines, sleep aids and sedatives may affect safe driving. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R53 | anchor: A24
Read prescription and package warnings about a medicine's effects before taking it. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R54 | anchor: A24
Illegal drugs can impair reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R55 | anchor: A24
The handbook associates marijuana use with more mistakes and trouble adapting to glare. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R56 | anchor: A24
For a first drug-impaired-driving conviction, the handbook lists a fine from 750 to 1000 dollars plus court costs. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R57 | anchor: A24
For a first drug-impaired-driving conviction, the handbook lists at least 48 jail hours or 100 community-service hours. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R58 | anchor: A24
The handbook describes license suspension after a first drug-impaired-driving conviction. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R59 | anchor: A24
Later drug-impaired-driving convictions carry more severe penalties. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R60 | anchor: A24
Do not combine drinking alcohol with other drugs. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R61 | anchor: A24
Combining alcohol and drugs can magnify impairment and cause serious illness or death. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R62 | anchor: A24
Driving experience does not make alcohol-impaired or drug-impaired driving safe. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R63 | anchor: A24
Even a cold, stiff neck, cough or sore leg can affect driving. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R64 | anchor: A24
If illness makes you unwell, ask someone else to drive. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec03-R65 | anchor: A25
Ask a doctor about a health condition that may prevent safe driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R66 | anchor: A25
Strong emotions can disrupt thinking, attention and information processing while driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R67 | anchor: A25
Being very worried, excited, afraid, angry or depressed may prevent safe driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R68 | anchor: A25
If angry or excited, stay off the road until you calm down. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R69 | anchor: A25
A short walk or nap can help an angry or excited person settle before driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R70 | anchor: A25
When worried or upset, keep attention on driving rather than the upsetting issue. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R71 | anchor: A25
The handbook allows listening to the radio as a calming aid only when it does not distract from driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R72 | anchor: A25
An impatient driver should allow extra trip time and leave earlier. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R73 | anchor: A25
Do not dart through traffic or drive faster than the traffic flow because of impatience. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec03-R74 | anchor: A25
Having another person drive is an option when emotions interfere with safe driving. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0025]
